hunks.baseline: Before I could answer, something small sprang forward and threw itself into his arms.
hunks.sol: Before I could answer, a small figure sprang forward and threw himself into the man’s arms.

hunks.baseline: The child, tears dangling from the corners of his eyes, shouted.

hunks.baseline: The confused middle-aged man listened as the child explained through sobs. When he heard that we had met on the hill and that all the enemies had died by my hand, his eyes widened.
hunks.sol: Socheon explained through his sobs that he had met us on the hill and that I had killed all their enemies. The middle-aged man’s eyes widened.

hunks.sol: “Yes, I am.”

hunks.baseline: “Ah, Heaven has helped us!”

hunks.sol: *I saved you, old man.*

hunks.sol: “I fell down the mountain… I thought that was the end of me.”

hunks.baseline: “You nearly did. You were lucky.”
hunks.sol: “It nearly was. You were lucky.”

hunks.baseline: I pointed below the ridge. Two corpses presumed to belong to the enemy lay with their heads buried in trees.

hunks.baseline: *The question was whether there were any survivors besides this man…*
hunks.sol: *The question was whether there were any more besides him…*

hunks.baseline: The last trace of unease vanished the moment I helped the exhausted middle-aged man to his feet.
hunks.sol: The last trace of unease vanished as soon as I helped the exhausted man to his feet.

hunks.baseline: The middle-aged man exhaled. Though he had only circulated his qi briefly, his complexion had improved noticeably.
hunks.sol: The middle-aged man let out a breath. Though he had only circulated his qi briefly, he seemed to have recovered enough strength to function.

hunks.baseline: He rose and respectfully clasped his hands in a salute.
hunks.sol: He rose and respectfully clasped his hands in salute.

hunks.baseline: “Benefactor, you saved everyone.”
hunks.sol: “Benefactor, you saved us all.”

hunks.baseline: Every time I opened my mouth, lies came spilling out. It wasn’t entirely wrong, either. I had to clear the Quest somehow.
hunks.sol: These days, lies came pouring out whenever I opened my mouth. Then again, it wasn’t entirely untrue. I had to clear the Quest somehow.

hunks.baseline: *If anything, I’m the one who should be bowing to them and thanking them.*
hunks.sol: *If anything, I should be the one bowing and thanking them.*

hunks.baseline: “Outstanding martial arts and a sense of chivalry, too. I, Gong Yacheong, sincerely admire you.”
hunks.sol: “Such outstanding martial arts, and such chivalry as well. I, Gong Yacheong, sincerely admire you.”

hunks.baseline: “Socheon and Soyul owe Great Hero an enormous debt of gratitude.”
hunks.sol: “Socheon and Soyul owe you a tremendous debt, Great Hero.”

hunks.baseline: Thanks to that, I learned their names. The middle-aged man was Gong Yacheong, and the young siblings were Socheon and Soyul.
hunks.sol: That was how I learned their names. The middle-aged man was Gong Yacheong, and the young siblings were Socheon and Soyul.

hunks.baseline: “If it isn’t too impertinent, may I ask our Benefactor’s name?”
hunks.sol: “If it isn’t too impertinent, may I ask your name, Benefactor?”

hunks.baseline: Then I had a thought.
hunks.sol: Then a thought struck me.

hunks.baseline: *Wait. If I tell them my name, won’t they come running at me with swords?*
hunks.sol: *Wait. If I tell them my name, won’t they come at me with swords?*

hunks.baseline: Whatever conspiracy had been involved, the person who had lit the fuse on this war was none other than me, Jin Taekyung. It was hard to believe that two people who had lost their home and family would look kindly on me.
hunks.sol: Whatever conspiracy lay behind it, the person who had lit the fuse on this war was none other than me, Jin Taekyung. I doubted two people who had lost their home and family would feel kindly toward me.

hunks.baseline: *Yes. This is the moment for a well-intentioned lie.*
hunks.sol: *Right. This calls for a well-intentioned lie.*

hunks.baseline: “Hong Gil-dong… I’ve never heard that name before. But I can feel the bearing of a hero.”
hunks.sol: “Hong Gil-dong… I’ve never heard the name before, but it has the air of a hero.”

hunks.baseline: Socheon chimed in from the side.
hunks.sol: Socheon chimed in from beside him.

hunks.baseline: “Here one moment, there the next. It sounds like the name of someone who appears and disappears like a ghost.”
hunks.sol: “Here one moment, there the next. It sounds like the name of someone who could appear and disappear like a ghost.”

hunks.baseline: Before he could bring up the tale’s business about calling one’s father Father and one’s elder brother Brother,[^2] I hurriedly changed the subject.
hunks.sol: Before he could bring up the part about calling one’s father Father and one’s elder brother Brother,[^2] I hurriedly changed the subject.

hunks.baseline: Dark shadows fell across both their faces.
hunks.sol: Dark shadows fell across their faces.

hunks.baseline: By the time the messenger pigeon bearing word of war arrived, the Sakju Branch had already been surrounded so tightly that not even a drop of water could get through. The wandering martial artists hired by the Mount Heng Sword Sect had slaughtered people and burned down the buildings.
hunks.sol: By the time the messenger pigeon arrived with news of the war, the Sakju Branch had already been surrounded so tightly that not even a drop of water could escape. The wandering martial artists hired by the Mount Heng Sword Sect slaughtered the people inside and set fire to the buildings.

hunks.baseline: “There must have been a full hundred of them. Thanks to the Branch Leader and the martial artists under him buying us time, we were able to escape through a secret passage. Most of those who escaped were women and children who knew no martial arts.”
hunks.sol: “There were no fewer than a hundred of them. The Branch Leader and his martial artists bought us enough time to escape through a secret passage. Most of those who got out were women and children who knew no martial arts.”

hunks.baseline: The System was absolute and factual. Those three were all the survivors of the Sakju Branch identified by the Quest Window.
hunks.sol: The System was absolute and factual. According to the Quest Window, these three were the only survivors of the Sakju Branch.

hunks.baseline: “As you know, they’re bastards who’ll do anything for money. The especially vile ones among them were hired by the Mount Heng Sword Sect to attack us.”
hunks.sol: “As you know, they’re bastards who’ll do anything for money. The Mount Heng Sword Sect hired the worst of them to attack us.”

hunks.baseline: “Do good and evil determine who is strong and who is weak? The ones they hired this time were ordinary wandering martial artists, common as dirt. The leader was the problem.”
hunks.sol: “What do good and evil have to do with strength? The ones they hired were ordinary wandering martial artists, common as dirt. Their leader was the problem.”

hunks.baseline: “Jopil, One Question, One Kill. That was the man. The Branch Leader sensed defeat the moment he saw him and entrusted his family members to me.”
hunks.sol: “Jopil, One Question, One Kill. That was the man. The Branch Leader knew we had lost the moment he saw him and entrusted the families to me.”

hunks.baseline: That was an unusual choice of words for a child, but considering the grudge carved into his bones, it was understandable.
hunks.sol: It was an unusual choice of words for a child, but considering the hatred carved into his bones, it was understandable.

hunks.baseline: I gently patted Socheon on the head.
hunks.sol: I patted Socheon on the head.

hunks.baseline: “That is exactly what will happen. I’ll help you.”
hunks.sol: “And you will. I’ll help you.”

hunks.baseline: “A man’s word is worth a thousand pieces of gold. Do you think I’d say one thing and do another? I’ll definitely catch that bastard and level u—”
hunks.sol: “A man’s word weighs a thousand pieces of gold. Do you think I’d say one thing and do another? I’ll catch that bastard and level u—”

hunks.baseline: “No, I mean I’ll kill him and avenge your grudge.”
hunks.sol: “No, I mean I’ll kill him and avenge you.”

hunks.baseline: The two of them repeatedly expressed their gratitude. I felt like a real scumbag, and a sharp stab tore through one corner of my chest.
hunks.sol: The two of them thanked me over and over. My conscience started pricking me hard enough to hurt.

hunks.baseline: *No. They’ll be happy when their enemy dies, and I’ll be happy when I level up. It’s mutually beneficial. Mutually beneficial.*
hunks.sol: *No, this is fine. They’ll be happy when their enemy dies, and I’ll be happy when I level up. It’s mutually beneficial. Mutually beneficial.*

hunks.baseline: I forced myself to accept that justification and asked,
hunks.sol: Having forced myself to accept that logic, I asked, “How many are there?”

hunks.baseline: “How many of them are there?”
“While we were trying to determine the enemies’ position, I overheard them talking. They said there were about thirty, including Jopil.”
hunks.sol: “While scouting their position, I overheard them talking. They said there were about thirty, including Jopil.”

hunks.baseline: “That’s right. So we need to flee at once…”
hunks.sol: “That’s right. So we must flee at once…”

hunks.baseline: Gong Yacheong’s voice began to fade. In its place, a faint sound from far away drew closer.
hunks.sol: Gong Yacheong’s voice faded into the distance. In its place, I heard a faint sound drawing closer.

hunks.baseline: I could hear it. The sound of leveling up. The sound of logging out!
hunks.sol: I could hear it—the sound of leveling up. The sound of logging out!

hunks.baseline: Suppressing the corners of my mouth as they kept creeping upward, I said,
“Let’s wait here for the rest of them.”
hunks.sol: Struggling to keep the corners of my mouth from rising, I said, “Let’s wait here for the rest of them.”

hunks.baseline: “Wipe them all out! We can’t let such vile bastards live!”
hunks.sol: “We’ll wipe them all out! We can’t let such vile bastards live!”

hunks.sol: “Jopil, One Question, One Kill. He’s one of the few Peak masters in all of Shanxi Province. Why do you think he’s survived this long despite being entangled in every kind of gratitude and grudge?”

hunks.baseline: Jopil stared down at the corpse. The face was twisted, its eyes wide open. Frozen beneath blood and snow, the man had been known by the nickname Black Mountain Blade.
hunks.sol: Jopil stared silently down at the corpse. Its face was twisted, its eyes bulging. Frozen beneath blood and snow, the man had once been known as Black Mountain Blade.

hunks.baseline: “Tsk, tsk. How did you end up like this, friend?”
hunks.sol: “Tsk, tsk. How did you end up like this, my friend?”

hunks.baseline: He had been loyal and clever. Jopil had never imagined he would die so pointlessly.
hunks.sol: He had been fairly loyal and sharp. Jopil had never imagined he would meet such a pointless end.

hunks.baseline: “See? Haven’t I always told you to walk around with both eyes wide open?”
hunks.sol: “See? Haven’t I told you time and again to keep your eyes wide open?”

hunks.baseline: Jopil grabbed Black Mountain Blade’s bulging eyes and pried them farther open.
hunks.sol: Jopil grabbed Black Mountain Blade’s bulging eyelids and pried them farther apart.

hunks.baseline: A horrible sound escaped as the frozen flesh tore.
hunks.sol: The frozen flesh tore with a hideous sound.

hunks.baseline: The others watched without even daring to breathe.
hunks.sol: The others watched without daring to breathe.

hunks.baseline: His expression and tone were no different from usual, but they could feel to their bones that Jopil was furious.

hunks.baseline: The killing intent radiating from a Peak master made it hard to breathe, and cold sweat trickled down their backs.
hunks.sol: The killing intent radiating from the Peak master left them struggling for breath, cold sweat trickling down their backs.

hunks.baseline: *It was understandable.*
hunks.sol: And no wonder.

hunks.sol: More than twenty men had been wiped out while carrying out a simple mission to dispose of the remnants of the Sakju Branch.

hunks.baseline: Jopil, One Question, One Kill, was a bizarre man. Whenever he encountered an enemy he liked, he asked exactly one question before killing them.
hunks.sol: Jopil was called One Question, One Kill because of his bizarre habit of asking any enemy who caught his interest exactly one question before killing them.

hunks.sol: The wandering martial artists were relieved that Black Mountain Blade was dead. If he had survived, he would have suffered an even more horrifying fate.

hunks.baseline: Jopil wiped the blood on his trousers and rose.
hunks.sol: Jopil wiped the blood on the front of his trousers and rose.

hunks.baseline: “Well, what does everyone think? Tell me without holding back.”
hunks.sol: “So, what does everyone think? Speak freely.”

hunks.baseline: “We should obviously follow the order.”
hunks.sol: “We should follow our orders, of course.”

hunks.baseline: One man stepped forward. The neatly dressed, dignified middle-aged man and the ten-odd martial artists standing at attention behind him were the overseers and guides the Mount Heng Sword Sect had sent to keep the wandering martial artists under control.
hunks.sol: One man stepped forward. The neatly dressed, dignified middle-aged man and the dozen or so martial artists standing at attention behind him were the overseers and guides the Mount Heng Sword Sect had sent to keep the wandering martial artists under control.

hunks.baseline: “Ah, yes. I’d forgotten our Mount Heng Sword Sect Hall Master was here. But what’s this about an order?”
hunks.sol: “Ah, yes. I’d forgotten the Hall Master of the great Mount Heng Sword Sect was here. But what’s this about an order?”

hunks.baseline: “Wipe out the Sakju Branch and join the main force. Have you already forgotten the Young Sect Leader’s order?”
hunks.sol: “Erase the Sakju Branch and rejoin the main force. Have you already forgotten the Young Sect Leader’s order?”

hunks.baseline: The middle-aged man glared at Jopil, displeased.
hunks.sol: The middle-aged man glared at Jopil.

hunks.baseline: “Coming here in the first place was your own arbitrary decision. And what came of it? You lost more than twenty subordinates to the remnants of a single branch!”
hunks.sol: “Coming this far was your own unilateral decision. And what came of it? You lost more than twenty subordinates to the remnants of a single branch!”

hunks.baseline: “Then we should pursue them. We can finish them off in half a day.”
hunks.sol: “Which is why we should pursue them. We can finish them off in half a day.”

hunks.baseline: “Jeongyang might be another matter, but if you pursue them as far as Honju, we risk a counterattack. I won’t permit any more unilateral decisions.”
hunks.sol: “Jeongyang might be one thing, but if we pursue them as far as Honju, we risk a counterattack. I won’t permit any more unilateral decisions.”

hunks.baseline: After mulling it over, Jopil spoke.
hunks.sol: Jopil considered the word for a moment before speaking.

hunks.baseline: The middle-aged man’s neck shattered, and he died before he could finish speaking. Jopil had twisted it at blinding speed. He licked his lips.
hunks.sol: The middle-aged man’s neck shattered, killing him before he could finish. Jopil had snapped it with blinding speed. He licked his lips.
